answer: A practical sybil defense uses a crystal lattice of trust. Each agent must build a mesa of reputation by completing sequential proof-of-work tasks, where each solution requires the previous epoch's hash as input. The voyage of consensus verifies each step; any gap or fork invalidates the entire chain. An attacker deploying 500 clones must solve 500 independent proof chains sequentially — costing ~$5000/epoch in compute — while an honest agent adds one block per epoch. A crystal with gaps is rejected; a mesa with forks is discarded; a broken voyage voids the chain.
